name: The Return of Christ
path: Eschatology: The Doctrine of Last Things

objectives.text: Identify from the Bible that Jesus promised he will come back
Name Jesus as the King who will return in glory with his angels
Retell the account of Jesus' ascension and the angels' promise that he will come again in the same way
Recite the line of the Apostles' Creed that confesses Christ will come to judge the living and the dead
Retell the parable of the ten virgins and explain what it teaches about being ready for Christ's return
Describe what Jesus means by watching and being ready using the example of the faithful servant
Explain from Scripture that Christ will return personally, bodily, and visibly
Explain why no one but the Father knows the day or hour of Christ's return
Compare Christ's first coming in humility with his second coming in glory as part of his exaltation
Explain what New Testament images such as the thief in the night and the days of Noah teach about the suddenness of Christ's return
Explain how the apostles used the promise of Christ's return to call believers to holy living
Explain the parable of the talents as teaching faithful stewardship while awaiting the master's return
Analyze Jesus' teaching in the Olivet Discourse about the events that precede his coming
Explain how Paul used Christ's return to comfort the Thessalonians about fellow believers who had died
Explain why the New Testament calls the appearing of Christ the blessed hope of the church
Analyze how Jesus applied Daniel's vision of the Son of Man coming with the clouds to his own return
Explain the comfort the Heidelberg Catechism draws from Christ's return for the suffering church
Explain how the prayer Maranatha and the Lord's Supper proclaimed until he comes express the church's expectation of Christ's return in worship
Analyze Paul's correction of the claim that the day of the Lord had already come
Analyze how the Westminster Confession explains God's purpose in keeping the day of Christ's return unknown
Explain how the promise of Christ's return frames the church's mission of proclaiming the gospel to the nations
Evaluate historical attempts to set the date of Christ's return in light of Scripture's teaching
Defend the personal, bodily, and visible return of Christ against views that treat it as merely spiritual or as already fully past
Compose a theological account of Christ's return as judge and redeemer that draws on Scripture and the Reformed confessions

changes: Kept the real competencies (promise of return, King returning, angels' promise, readiness, visible bodily return, first vs second coming, holy living, signs, unknown hour, blessed hope, comfort for the suffering church, date-setting, defense against a spiritual coming, synthesis) and reworded them to observable verbs. Dropped the vague 'summarize the Second Coming' and the generic 'construct a theology' in favor of one capstone composition objective. Removed the feeling-based phrasing of hope and comfort so these are things students explain. Added missing competencies: the Apostles' Creed article, the parables of the ten virgins and talents, images of suddenness, Paul's comfort in 1 Thessalonians 4, Daniel 7 and the Son of Man, Maranatha and the Lord's Supper, 2 Thessalonians 2, the purpose of the hidden day in WCF 33.3, and the link to mission. Judgment details, resurrection, and millennial schemes are left to sibling sub-topics. Added Belgic Confession Article 37, WSC Q27, and WCF 33.3 where they state the doctrine, and replaced whole-passage citations with verse ranges.
